# shopping-cart

An in-memory `ShoppingCart` class for Node.js. The starting code in `src/cart.js`
had five bugs; this repo fixes them and adds regression tests that fail on each
one.

## Usage

```js
const ShoppingCart = require('./src/cart');

const cart = new ShoppingCart();
cart.addItem('shirt', 25, 2);   // name, unit price, quantity
cart.addItem('socks', 5, 4);
cart.addItem('socks', 5, 2);    // same name: quantity becomes 6

cart.getItemCount();            // 2 (distinct line items)
cart.getTotal();                // 80

cart.applyDiscount(25);         // 25% off the whole cart
cart.getTotal();                // 60

cart.removeItem('socks');
cart.getTotal();                // 37.5
```

## API

| Method | Accepts | Throws |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addItem(name, price, quantity)` | `name`: non-empty string. `price`: finite number >= 0. `quantity`: positive safe integer. | `TypeError` for a wrong type, empty name, `NaN` or `Infinity`. `RangeError` for a negative price, a quantity below 1 or with a fractional part, or a merge that would go past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. |
| `removeItem(name)` | Name of an item in the cart. | `TypeError` for an invalid name. `Error` if the item is not in the cart. |
| `getTotal()` | — | — |
| `applyDiscount(percent)` | Finite number from 0 to 100 inclusive. Fractions are fine. | `TypeError` for a non-number, `NaN` or `Infinity`. `RangeError` outside 0-100. |
| `getItemCount()` | — | — |

Each method checks all its input before changing anything, so a call that throws
leaves the cart as it was.

## The five bugs

| # | Where | Bug | Fix | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `addItem` | Accepted negative prices and quantities. A negative quantity on an existing item quietly reduced it. | Validate name, price and quantity before any change. | `bug 1:` in `tests/cart.test.js` |
| 2 | `removeItem` | `i.name = name` assigned instead of comparing. The filter kept every item and renamed all of them. Removing a missing item did nothing. | Compare with `!==`. Throw if nothing matched. | `bug 2:` |
| 3 | `getTotal` | `i <= this.items.length` read one past the end, so every call threw `TypeError`, even on an empty cart. | Iterate with `for...of`, which has no index to get wrong. | `bug 3:` |
| 4 | `getTotal` | The discount was added to the total: 10% off 100 gave 110. | Subtract it. | `bug 4:` |
| 5 | `applyDiscount` | Stored any value. 150% gave a negative total, -10% raised the price, and `'10'` or `NaN` got in too. | Require a finite number from 0 to 100. | `bug 5:` |

To confirm the tests catch the bugs, the suite was run against mutants: the fixed
file with exactly one bug put back at a time, plus the original file as given.
Each mutant failed at least one test tagged with its bug number.

## Decisions where the spec was silent

- **Removing a missing item throws** instead of returning `false`. The other
  methods throw on bad input, and a silent no-op was part of bug 2.
- **Zero price is allowed** so free items work. **Zero quantity is rejected**
  because adding nothing is almost always a caller mistake.
- **Quantities must be integers.** Carts that sell by weight would need a
  different rule.
- **Adding an existing name keeps the first unit price** and only adds to the
  quantity, as the original code did. To change a price, remove the item and add
  it again.
- **Names match exactly.** They are case-sensitive and not Unicode-normalized, so
  `'café'` (NFC) and `'café'` (NFD) are different items. Normalize names
  before calling if that matters. Whitespace-only names are rejected, but names
  are not trimmed.
- **`applyDiscount` replaces the current discount**; it does not stack. Pass `0`
  to clear it.
- **`getItemCount` counts line items**, not units, as the original did.
- **`getTotal` is not rounded.** Decimal prices can give float results such as
  `0.30000000000000004`. Rounding to two places would assume a currency with
  cents, so formatting is left to the caller. For exact money arithmetic, store
  prices in integer minor units.
- **One source file.** The fix is small enough that splitting the validation
  helpers into their own module would add indirection without making anything
  easier to test.

## Development

Requires Node.js 20 or later.

```sh
npm install      # installs ESLint (tests use the built-in node:test runner)
npm test         # runs all tests
npm run lint     # runs ESLint
npm run check    # lint, then tests
```

Tests are in three files:

- `tests/cart.test.js`: each public method, plus the `bug N:` regression tests.
- `tests/cart.edge-cases.test.js`: unicode and very long names, numeric limits,
  unusual input types, failed calls leaving state unchanged, separate carts, and
  10,000-item stress runs.
- `tests/cart.integration.test.js`: multi-step checkout flows, recovery after
  errors, and interleaved async callers sharing one cart.

content.text:
All five bugs in `src/cart.js` are fixed, and each has regression tests that fail when that bug is put back. Lint and all 101 tests pass (full gate run through `run-gate`).

**The bugs and fixes**

| # | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `addItem` accepted negative prices and quantities; a negative quantity on an existing item quietly reduced it | Name, price and quantity are checked before the cart changes. Wrong types throw `TypeError`, out-of-range values throw `RangeError` |
| 2 | `removeItem` used `i.name = name`, which kept every item and renamed all of them to the removed name; a missing item was silently ignored | Compares with `!==` and throws if the item isn't in the cart |
| 3 | `getTotal` looped with `<=`, so it threw on every call, even on an empty cart | Loops with `for...of`, so there's no index to get wrong |
| 4 | The discount was added: 10% off 100 gave 110 | Subtracts it |
| 5 | `applyDiscount` stored anything (150, -10, `'10'`, `NaN`) | Only accepts a finite number from 0 to 100 |
